messages:
dev-tej: Hey team — our master CI deploys started failing ~10:22 UTC with 403s when the job tries to call the Redwood API using the ci-deployer service account token. First seen on 2026-03-15.

infra-oncall: Can you paste the last 3 lines from the deploy job logs and the exact error body? Also which token the job is using (OIDC identity token vs SA impersonation)?

dev-tej: Logs:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json
{ "error": "permission denied: service account impersonation", "code": 403 }
```
The job uses the runner identity to impersonate projects/infra-prod/serviceAccounts/ci-deployer@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com via OIDC -> short-lived SA token.

maria: Recent change: gitlab-runner config was updated last week to request 5m identity tokens (ttl=300s). Our impersonation window for the SA token creator flow is 10m, but there was also an internal override on the token lifetime policy to 2m for that project. Could be a lifetime mismatch / early expiry.

alex: Quick check — does the CI runner's service account have iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator (or equivalent) on the ci-deployer SA? Run: `gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy ci-deployer@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=infra-prod` and look for the runner principal with roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator.

dev-tej: I ran the policy inspect, the binding exists for group:ci-runners@redwood-prod, role roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator. But the impersonation request log shows token exp is ~90s after issuance sometimes. I can paste the raw JWT header/payload if useful: `echo $TOKEN | awk -F'.' '{print $2}' | base64 -d` -> payload shows exp: 168945... (very short) and aud: "https://redwood.internal" which matches.

ops-luis: If exp is shorter than the time the backend checks (clock skew + processing delays), the API will reject it. Two quick mitigations: 1) increase the identity/token lifetime on the runner (to >= 10m), or 2) temporarily add a delegated API key to the CI job that bypasses SA impersonation for deploys (short-lived, rotate after). Longer-term: align runner TTL and project token lifetime policy.

maria: Another angle — some runners cache tokens and reuse them across stages. If the job reuses a token issued earlier, expiration edge cases happen. Ensure the job obtains a fresh token right before the call.

infra-oncall: For immediate triage: please try these repro steps in a shell on the runner host: 1) `gcloud auth print-identity-token --audiences=https://redwood.internal --time-format=unix` 2) `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.internal/v1/deploy` Capture response and token `exp` claim. Post output here (redact full tokens).

dev-tej: Ran the repro. Response same 403. Token payload excerpt: `{ "exp": 2098765445, "iat": 2098765145, "aud": "https://redwood.internal" }` — looks like exp only 5 minutes after iat in some runs, 3 minutes in others. Runner config shows `oidc: token_lifetime: 180` in some runners (legacy), new runners request 300. Manifest mismatch.

alex: Ok that explains variability. Two fixes: update runners to request 600s tokens and set project token lifetime min to 600s, OR change impersonation flow to verify token with more relaxed clock skew tolerance (undesirable). Also add a small retry with fresh token on 401/403 transient.

infra-bot: action taken: created infra-ticket #INF-4421 to standardize runner token_lifetime to 600s and audit SA token lifetime policy.

dev-tej: I temporarily bumped the runner job to request `token_lifetime: 600` and re-ran — deploy succeeded. Thanks.

ops-luis: Great. Follow-ups: 1) PR to runbook documenting required token_lifetime >= 600s for deploy jobs, 2) add a small client retry (obtain fresh token and retry once) for 401/403 with impersonation errors, 3) audit and rotate any long-lived keys if used.

maria: I'll own the runbook PR. infra-oncall please coordinate the IAM audit from INF-4421.

infra-oncall: Will do. Marking thread resolved for the deploy outage; keep this open for runbook + audit tasks.
